blogs.content: The Gorgias & Shopify Integration: 8 Standout Features Book a demo Blog Shopify The Gorgias & Shopify Integration: 8 Features Your Support Team Will Love 0 min - Holly Stanley Updated on June 30, 2026 - Created on January 28, 2025 Shopify Apps and Integrations No items found. Table of contents Heading 2 Heading 3 Want to provide Best-in-class CX to your Shoppers? Try Gorgias Free Now TL;DR Gorgias centralizes Shopify support in one platform. Agents view and update orders, customers, and refunds without leaving the helpdesk. Macros, Rules, and AI Agent automate personalized responses. Real-time Shopify data plus automation powers fast, on-brand support and pre-sale shopping help. Customers self-serve routine order questions. Order Management on Chat deflects "where's my order" tickets before they reach an agent. Support drives sales, not just resolutions. Brands on Gorgias turn conversations into conversions and track the revenue support generates. Managing customer support as a Shopify store owner can feel like juggling too many tools at once. Constantly switching tabs to look up orders, update customer information, or track returns wastes time your team doesn't have. Worse, it pulls them away from what actually moves the business: quick, personalized customer service that turns a question into a sale. Gorgias is the Conversational Commerce platform built for Shopify brands. Its Shopify integration keeps all your store data in one place, so your team spends less time toggling tabs and more time helping shoppers buy and stay. The result: faster responses, better service, and more revenue per conversation. Below, we break down the eight capabilities that make this integration worth setting up, each paired with a real use case. {{lead-magnet-1}} 1. View Shopify data in tickets What it does: Shopify order data shows up directly inside support tickets, so agents see order status, customer details, and transaction history without leaving the helpdesk. Use case: An agent handling a "Where's my order?" request can check tracking and update the customer in seconds. The fashion retailer Princess Polly used Gorgias's deep Shopify integration to give agents one screen for everything. Viewing and updating order data inside Gorgias, instead of switching between tabs, led to a 40% increase in efficiency , an 80% decrease in resolution time , and a 95% decrease in first response time . 2. Perform Shopify Actions What it does: Agents update Shopify order and customer data with Shopify Actions right inside Gorgias. Key features: Create a new order: Add existing products or custom items, apply discounts, modify quantities, add notes and tags, charge taxes, set the order as Paid or Pending, and email the invoice. Duplicate an order: Replicate an existing order and adjust as needed. Cancel or refund an order: Set quantities to refund, specify shipping refunds, give a reason, restock items, and notify the customer. Edit shipping address: Update the shipping address on an order. Insert product links: Drop product links or product cards into a ticket so customers can add to cart in one tap. Display the customer's cart: See exactly what's in the shopper's cart the moment they reach out on Chat. Use case: A shopper messages to swap a size right after ordering. The agent edits the order and reships the correct item without opening Shopify in a separate tab. Agents can perform Shopify Actions like duplicate an order directly from Gorgias. 3. Embed customer-specific Shopify data in Macros What it does: Build templated responses called Macros with dynamic Shopify variables that auto-fill customer-specific information. Key features: Dynamic variables: Macros pull real-time Shopify data like order status, tracking numbers, and customer details. Automated actions: Beyond inserting content, Macros can tag tickets, set statuses, or assign conversations, keeping similar inquiries handled consistently. Use case: A customer asks about their order. With one click, the agent applies a Macro that pulls the order status and expected delivery date into a fast, personalized reply. Try The World , a gourmet subscription brand, needed a Shopify integration that could keep up with rising ticket volume. After switching to Gorgias, they unified conversations and embedded Shopify data straight into Macros. Their team's output climbed to 120 tickets per day, up from 80 , with response times down to a single business day. Shopify data lets agents create Macros, templated responses with personalized data. 4. Share product information with Macros What it does: Macros with embedded Shopify data let agents share pre-sale information like product links, stock availability, and discount codes, turning prospective shoppers into buyers. Key features: Dynamic Shopify variables in Macros: Pull live product and inventory information into a reply. Pre-built responses for common questions: Templated answers for pre-sale inquiries, like direct product links or discount codes. Use case: A shopper asks whether a product is in stock in their size and color. The agent applies a Macro that pulls inventory details and adds a welcome code: "Hi [customer name], Great news, [product name] is in stock in the size and color you're after. You can grab it here: [Product Link]. Use WELCOME10 at checkout for 10% off your first order. Let me know if you have any other questions!" How it helps: Removes manual lookups and typing for agents. Gives shoppers accurate, real-time product information. Improves the odds of turning an inquiry into a sale. 5. Let customers self-serve order management in Chat What it does: With Gorgias Chat , customers track orders and manage purchases on their own, no agent needed. Key feature: Order Management automation: Customers get real-time order status and tracking right in the chat window. This deflects up to 30% of live chat inquiries. Use case: A customer wants to check on a recent purchase. They open Chat, enter their email and order number, and get instant shipping and delivery updates without waiting for an agent. How it helps: Automates routine questions so agents focus on complex issues. Lifts satisfaction with instant answers. Consolidates support in one place instead of scattering it across channels. 6. Use Shopify variables in Rules What it does: Rules paired with Shopify variables automate support tasks like routing, tagging, and prioritizing, for more consistency and less manual work. Key features: Automated tagging: Tag tickets based on Shopify data, such as flagging VIP customers or high-value orders. Smart routing: Send tickets to the right agent or team based on order value, customer segment, or product purchased. Prioritization: Push urgent or high-value conversations to the top of the queue automatically. Use case: A Rule detects when a customer's lifetime spend crosses your VIP threshold and routes their ticket to a senior agent with a VIP tag, so your best customers get your best service. ‍ Rules let you identify VIP customers using Shopify variables. 7. Track the revenue support generates What it does: Gorgias reporting measures how support interactions influence sales, so CX stops being a cost center and starts showing up as a revenue line. Key features: Tickets converted: The number of support tickets that led to a sale within five days of the ticket's creation. Conversion rate: The percentage of created tickets that resulted in sales. Total sales from support: Revenue from orders tied to converted tickets, adjusted for refunds and order changes. Find these under Statistics → Support Performance → Revenue in Gorgias. Built on data from 5,000+ brands. Explore how Loop can help you Optimize your commerce operations and unlock a new level of efficiency. Book a demo When you’re trying to build an ecommerce brand, it’s a lot easier if you take the blindfold off. Whether you’re a new business or a legacy brand, every step of your business strategy should be evidence-based. From generating sales to reengaging past shoppers to eliminating fraud, data can tell you how to make the most out of your operating budget – and if you’re not using it wisely (or at all), you’ll make critical mistakes that can be tough to recover from. When it comes to steering your ecommerce ship, generic analytics tools aren’t good enough. You need access to a specialized data intelligence platform that can look beyond your own store data to bring together a wealth of insights drawn from millions of ecommerce transactional data points. Discover how our new AI solution, Loop Intelligence , can help your brand scale faster, protect margins, and improve your CX with the use of sophisticated data analytics tools. Why generic AI won’t help Sure, you’ve got AI tools at your disposal. You might use CoPilot or Gemini to solve problems every day – and while they may be great for summarizing meeting notes or analyzing a spreadsheet, those solutions fall far short when it comes to generating data insights and recommendations that will truly move the needle for your ecommerce brand. Even if they’re trained to look at your own brand’s historical data, that’s all they’re looking at. They can’t see how your data compares against thousands of different brands in diverse verticals – so they’re likely to miss out on vital context that would help you determine the right course of action in any scenario. To build a sustainable business, you need to look beyond your own brand history, and pool from the collective wisdom of other ecommerce brands. Using an ecommerce-specific AI solution will help you generate insights to fuel your growth and protect your margins, while saving time on manual review. How ecommerce-specific AI works By using an AI model that’s been trained on specialized commerce data (including returns, shipping, carrier performance, fraud, product behavior, exchange patterns), you’ll be able to identify patterns across all your data – even if it’s not clear based on your own historical data. By drawing from a broader foundation that pulls together data points from thousands of brands, you’ll gain access to stronger predictive accuracy. For instance, you’ll be able to spot subtle red flags for fraud, even if your own business has never seen them before. Rather than let it slide by undetected, you’ll be able to immediately halt these transactions and submit them for manual review – protecting your business margins without negatively impacting the customer experience. That level of specialization is crucial for supporting your overall business performance and operational outcomes. Loop Intelligence: A category-defining example Trained on years of ecommerce data across thousands of businesses and millions of transactions, Loop Intelligence is the premier data analytics solution for ecommerce businesses. With a wealth of features to help you streamline your business and automate decisions based on data insights, you’ll be equipped with the tools you need to stay a step ahead of your competition. Here’s a look at how you can succeed with an ecommerce-focused AI solution: Revenue retention Our solution helps brands lift revenue retention from returns by 11%. By delivering data-backed product recommendations to customers considering exchanges, you’ll be able to improve your exchange rate and help customers find products they’ll love. Fraud prevention Loop Intelligence has uncovered patterns of returns abuse across millions of returns transactions, and can quickly spot warning signs of potential fraud or abuse in your return requests. We can immediately flag that transaction for manual review, helping you protect your margins and customer experience. Shipping optimization With our Dynamic Routing tools, you can set your priorities for return shipping to balance speed against cost. Our solution will instantly identify the carrier and specific route that fits your needs, so you can get inventory back in hand faster at a sustainable cost. Policy refinement Customers don’t all behave the same way. So why would you treat your best customers the same as you’d treat a known policy abuser? Loop can automatically set up and enforce dynamic policies based on customer behavior, so that you can ensure your best shoppers get the experience they deserve, while protecting your brand against abusers. Scalable automation Loop gives you the tools to make data-backed decisions about your post-purchase strategies – ensuring that you can choose the correct course of action every time without the need for manual intervention. That saves you time and money on CX, so you can scale your business faster and more efficiently. Using Loop Intelligence to tap into the right insights will help you curb costs, protect margins, and enhance your customer experience, so you can scale faster. Ready to see how we can help? blogs.content: Blog The EU withdrawal button is not the story. Build the process behind it. A note for US brands selling into Europe The big picture of the EU withdrawal button For information purposes only. This article does not constitute legal advice. Compliance with applicable regulations remains the responsibility of the retailer, and retailers should seek advice from their own legal team on their specific obligations. Why the EU withdrawal button reveals your operating model As of 19 June 2026, retailers selling into the EU face a clearer standard for how consumers exercise their right of withdrawal. The principle is simple: Withdrawing from a purchase should be as easy as making it. That sounds like a user interface requirement. It is more than that. The visible part is a button. The real challenge is everything that follows. Once a customer clicks “withdraw,” the operational questions begin. Which order is affected? Which items are included? Is the request for the full order or only part of it? Is the withdrawal still within the valid period? Has fulfillment already started? Can the shipment still be stopped, or does the retailer need to move directly into a return flow? This is why the withdrawal button matters beyond compliance. It reveals how well a retailer’s post-purchase operations are structured. If the process behind the button depends on inbox triage, manual review, and disconnected tools, the experience becomes harder than it should be for customers and more expensive than it should be for teams. The answer to the EU withdrawal button is in your returns portal That is also why the most practical answer may sit in an unexpected place: the returns portal. At first glance, using a returns portal to support withdrawal can seem counterintuitive. Withdrawal is a legal right. Returns are usually framed as a logistics workflow. In practice, the overlap is significant. The order data is already there. Customers can identify the relevant purchase without friction. Eligible items can be surfaced directly. Partial withdrawal can be handled in a structured way. Confirmation can be sent immediately. And where goods are already in motion, the next step often still involves return logistics, including clear instructions and, where needed, a return label. How parcelLab supports the EU withdrawal button in practice This is not theoretical. parcelLab has already helped several retailers operationalize this process. We have set up withdrawal reasons so they appear only within the relevant time window, configured confirmation emails that acknowledge the withdrawal and provide next steps, enabled instructions and labels where required, and updated the customer communications that parcelLab sends on the retailer’s behalf. In other words, the conversation does not stop at the button. We help retailers make the process behind it work. Seen this way, the returns portal stops being a narrow returns tool. It becomes part of a broader post-purchase service layer. See how the withdrawal flow is configured Read the docs Don’t just add the Withdrawal button. Build the process behind it. That shift is worth paying attention to. For years, ecommerce teams focused most of their innovation on conversion. Regulation, customer expectations, and operational pressure are now pushing more attention to what happens after the buy button. Withdrawal requests, delivery claims, damage claims, warranty cases, and returns all belong to the same reality: customers do not experience these as separate workflows. Customers experience them as moments when a brand either makes resolution easy or creates more effort. The retailers that respond well to this change will not be the ones that add the required button fastest. They will be the ones that treat the requirement as a design prompt for the entire post-purchase journey. The button may be the legal trigger. The real work is building a process that is clear for the customer, structured for internal teams, and connected to the systems that determine what can actually happen next. A note for US brands selling into Europe For US brands, there is an additional lesson here. Selling into Europe means operating in a market where consumer regulation shapes product and process decisions in a very direct way. This is not a future edge case. It is part of the operating environment. In that context, there is value in working with a partner that understands those requirements from the outset and is already prepared to support them in practice. The big picture of the EU withdrawal button As always, the legal framework still sits with the retailer. Technology can support the flow, remove friction, and make the process operationally manageable. It should not be mistaken for legal advice or legal sign-off. The withdrawal button is not only a compliance obligation. It is a signal that post-purchase experience is becoming a more strategic part of ecommerce operations. Retailers that understand that will do more than meet the rule. They will build better systems around it. If you are selling into the EU and want the process behind the button to work as well as the button itself, parcelLab can help you set it up inside the returns portal you already run. Your questions, answered What does the EU withdrawal button rule require, and when does it apply? It comes from Directive (EU) 2023/2673, which amends the Consumer Rights Directive (2011/83/EU). From 19 June 2026, retailers selling to EU consumers online must provide a clearly labeled electronic withdrawal function, available throughout the 14-day window, with a confirmation step and an automatic confirmation sent on a durable medium such as email. Is the withdrawal button just our returns page? No. A withdrawal is a legal act that cancels the contract; a return is the logistics that follow. The withdrawal function has to be a distinct, clearly labeled step, not a generic “returns” or “contact us” link. Your returns portal supports the operational handling once a withdrawal is triggered. We’re a US brand. Does this apply to us? Generally yes, if you sell to EU consumers but the specifics depend on how your business operates in those markets, so it’s worth checking with your legal team What happens if we are not ready? Penalties are set by each member state and can be significant, and the cooling-off window can extend well beyond the standard 14 days. This is general information, not legal advice. How does parcelLab support withdrawal requests? Within your existing returns portal, we configure a dedicated withdrawal reason that appears only within the valid window, surface eligible items, handle partial withdrawals, send confirmation and instructions including a label where needed, and pass the request to your systems through the same channels as other returns. It works on both Returns Portal versions. Note that the Returns Portal handles the withdrawal form and flow, but yo...

blogs.title: K:LDN 2026: The Full Recap – Klaviyo
blogs.author: Eve Rouse
blogs.content: Five years in, and K:LDN keeps getting bigger and better. Over 1,000 marketers, operators and brand builders flooded Tobacco Dock on 30th June for the fifth edition of Klaviyo's flagship London event. Some flew to be there—others arrived by Klaviyo-wrapped taxis… What followed was a day packed with everything from mainstage keynotes and Klaviyo customer panels, to product deep-dive sessions and customer education workshops. If you were there, you already know it was a day worth clearing your calendar for. If you weren’t, here’s a glimpse at what went down. Setting the scene Ben Jackson, managing director EMEA at Klaviyo, opened the day with a welcome address before handing over to Klaviyo co-founder and co-CEO Andrew Bialecki and CMO Jamie Domenici. Andrew and Jamie set out their vision for the next era of B2C: the autonomous CRM, where data, intelligence, and agents come together so brands can focus on outcomes rather than operations. Joining them on stage was Chano Fernandez, co-CEO at Klaviyo, and Thomas Davis, chief customer data and digital DTC officer at KIKO Milano , for a candid conversation about what clear leadership actually looks like when everything is changing at once, and how customer relationships become the thing that holds it all together. Across the venue While the sessions were only just getting started, the venue itself was already alive. Activations included: A beauty room featuring products and treatments from Wonderskin , CurrentBody , Living Proof , and Manucurist , plus freebies for all. A sports activation offering personalised Castore football shirts, printed on-site. A nod to the World Cup in full swing. An immersive window display showcasing products from iconic fashion brands in Klaviyo's roster, including Dr. Martens , Paul Smith , and Fiorucci , to name but a few. A music-inspired Hall of Fame featuring Klaviyo clients as record covers, complete with QR codes to their case studies. There was no shortage of things to see, try and take home. The breakouts have begun: Skin Rocks, Fiorucci, and more With the opening keynote done, seven sessions kicked off simultaneously across the venue. Gemma Stevenson, chief commercial officer at Skin Rocks , joined Kelly Thacker, VP of product marketing at Klaviyo, to talk about what it takes to scale a brand built on radical honesty in one of retail's noisiest categories. Fiorucci CDO Alberto Nicotra sat down with Emily McEvilly, chief customer officer at Klaviyo, for a conversation on what it actually looks like to take a cultural icon into accessible luxury for a new generation. A panel on what it really takes to build customer relationships on your own terms was brought together by Jake Cohen, VP and head of industry strategy at Klaviyo. Joining him was Kirsty Tansey, senior director of growth at Gozney , Alannah Murphy, senior CRM manager at Virgin Experience Days , and Amy Last, marketing director at Must Have Ideas . Over in the product lounge, a dedicated space for deep-dive platform sessions, Karisa Tate, lead PMM for Klaviyo Service , kicked things off by making the case for post-purchase support as a revenue driver, not a cost centre. She walked through how Klaviyo's Customer Agent handles returns, surfaces recommendations, restores loyalty points, and enriches customer profiles, all within a single conversation. Meanwhile, three customer education sessions ran in parallel: Vivian Asonye, senior customer education specialist at Klaviyo, and Brett Bernstein, product manager and Gatsby founder at Klaviyo, covered how to turn Instagram engagement into owned subscribers using Klaviyo Social Marketing . Emily Shea, principal customer education specialist at Klaviyo, tackled what your owned channel strategy should look like in a world where AI is increasingly shaping how customers discover brands. Melody Flumendorf, customer education specialist at Klaviyo, made the case for WhatsApp as a serious revenue channel for marketers ready to go beyond the inbox. The product headlines Attendees reconvened on the main stage for the product roadmap session after lunch, eager to see what Klaviyo had been cooking up. Andrew, Kelly and Karisa opened with a number that set the tone: 475+ features shipped since K:LDN 2025. But that was just the context. Here are the highlights. Composer enters public beta Klaviyo's next generation AI marketing agent, Composer , officially moved into public beta that day. Built on a brand's own customer data, performance history, and business goals, it identifies opportunities, recommends the next best action, and takes a campaign from prompt to launch-ready in minutes. Every recommendation is grounded in your actual account data: your flows, your segments, your campaign history, your brand voice. And nothing launches without human approval. Klaviyo Social Marketing: generally available 7th July Klaviyo Social Marketing was announced as moving to general availability on 7th July. It connects Instagram DMs, comments, and mentions directly to Klaviyo profiles, turning followers into subscribers you actually own. Set up a keyword-triggered auto-reply, capture a consented email or mobile number, and that follower is ready to enter your welcome flow. Customer Agent now speaks more than 100 languages Klaviyo's Customer Agent now automatically detects a shopper's language and responds in that language, across web chat, email, SMS, and WhatsApp. French, German, Spanish, Italian, and more than 100 other languages. No setup required. One configuration. Back to the breakouts: REFY Beauty, Castore, Clarks, and more Fresh off the product announcements, attendees spread across the venue for another round of parallel breakout sessions. Pia Tomlinson, VP of sales EMEA at Klaviyo, brought together three of the biggest brands in beauty right now for one of the most popular sessions of the day: Kate Poyser, senior CRM and loyalty manager at REFY Beauty , Kathleen Loftus, marketing director at Sculpted by Aimee , and Michelle Hurney, head of CRM at Wonderskin . The topic: how you take a customer who found you through a viral moment and turn them into someone who stays. Meanwhile, Kev McFadyen, CMO at Castore , sat down with Byron Goodman, senior director of EMEA mid-market and large enterprise at Klaviyo, to talk about what it actually takes to go from British start-up to near billion-pound global sportswear brand in under a decade. And Mario Protano, director of performance marketing at Clarks , joined Ameet Shah, senior director of EMEA customer success at Klaviyo, to get into the detail of rebuilding a 200-year-old brand's digital programme from the ground up. The product lounge also carried its energy into the afternoon, with a session that unpacked why bringing email, SMS, WhatsApp, and social together on one platform changes the game. Mindy Regnell, head of global market intelligence at Klaviyo, Deja Amato, product marketing at Klaviyo, and Kelsey Capps, product management at Klaviyo, were joined by Klaviyo agency partner Midge Hazewinkel, director of CRM at Domaine , to bring the real-world perspective. The education track continued: Severine Chaari, senior customer education specialist at Klaviyo, ran a hands-on session on Composer, fresh out of private beta, walking through how to turn AI-surfaced insights into measurable action. Vivian hosted Isabella Howarth, CRM and email specialist at Daals , who shared how she's using Klaviyo Social Marketing to turn Instagram engagement into owned subscribers and repeat buyers. The final block: Fashion, football, and enterprise transformation After a short break, more sessions kicked off across the venue, with the fashion panel pulling in one of the biggest crowds of the day. James White, senior director of partnerships EMEA at Klaviyo, brought together three of the most culturally relevant fashion brands around right now: Lisa Nielsen, senior digital marketing manager at Victoria Beckham , Jamie Degiorgio, digital director at Casab...

blogs.title: Klaviyo AI Agents Take On the Campaign, the Ticket, and Social Growth
blogs.author: Kelly Thacker
blogs.content: For years, "AI in your marketing stack" mostly meant a tool that suggested a segment or predicted what a customer might buy. Useful, but you were still the one doing the work: writing the brief, drafting the copy for each channel, lining up the timing, and answering the same "where's my order" question for the hundredth time. This quarter, that changes for Klaviyo customers. Now, Composer builds the campaign. Customer Agent resolves the ticket. Klaviyo Social Marketing turns followers into subscribers, then finds your top-performing content and the creators most worth partnering with. The full funnel production work that used to fill your week now runs on its own, grounded in your customer data, and nothing goes live without your sign-off. The agents do the work, you set the direction. Here’s what we launched, and how it works. Composer is now in public beta Klaviyo's AI marketing agent, Composer, is now in public beta. Describe the outcome you want in plain language, and Composer builds a complete campaign, grounded in your customer data and past performance, ready for you to review in minutes. Try "spring reactivation for customers who haven't purchased in 90 days, email and SMS, fresh tone," and it builds the audience, drafts the copy for each channel, coordinates the timing, and stages the send. You refine in follow-up messages and approve. Nothing goes live without you. The difference is where Composer starts. A generic AI tool hears "win back lapsed customers" and writes a discount email that could belong to anyone. Composer is built inside Klaviyo, so it already knows who counts as lapsed for your business, what those customers respond to, and which brand rules to follow. You get a campaign that's ready to run. Klaviyo customers get free credits to start, so you can build real campaigns against your own data right now. Get started. Customer Agent becomes a platform you can build on Customer Agent launched as an AI service agent. This quarter, it became a platform you can build on . It still runs on the same profile as your marketing programs. When a customer reaches out, it already knows their order history, loyalty status, and purchase behavior, so it can resolve and recommend in the same conversation. Pre-built skills for order tracking, returns, recommendations, and loyalty mean you're live from day one. And, Customer Agent is driving real business results. Naked Wardrobe reached 86% autonomous resolution within 90 days. NANUK saw a 100% increase in product recommendation, return, and exchange queries resolved within 90 days. Customer Agent resolves 65% of questions automatically. What's new is how much you can now build yourself. Conversational Agent Builder With the new Conversational Agent Builder, you describe what you want in plain language, and Klaviyo builds it for you. A running brand describes a "Find My Perfect Gear" quiz, and Klaviyo builds the entire experience: the questions, the logic, and the recommendations, with no engineering or manual work required. The quiz can also enrich your customer profiles as it runs. When a shopper tells the agent their favorite size, color, or activity, those details write straight back to their Klaviyo profile in real time, so every follow-up message and marketing email can speak to what they actually told you. Once it's built, test it before a single customer sees it. Run simulations and see how the agent responds. If something's off, click "Improve," describe the fix, and it updates itself. Pre-built connectors and open APIs Pre-built connectors let the agent act in the systems you already run, so it doesn't just talk about a subscription change, it makes the change. And the open APIs mean Customer Agent isn't limited to Shopify . If you run a headless or fully custom storefront, you can embed the agent right into it, so the same resolve-and-recommend experience shows up wherever your customers already shop. Customer Agent now speaks more than 100 languages Customer Agent now also speaks your customers' language, more than 100 of them, across web chat, email, SMS, RCS, and WhatsApp. This is what B2C AI service looks like when it's built on your data. Get started with Customer Agent now. More access to Klaviyo Social Marketing You built that following on your social platforms, but you don't really own it. One algorithm change or one lost account, and the audience you worked for is gone. That’s because your social followers don't belong to you. Your subscribers do, and Klaviyo Social Marketing is how you turn more of those followers into subscribers, turning social engagement into customer growth. Klaviyo Social Marketing connects what happens on social platforms, like Instagram DMs, comments, and mentions, directly to your unified Klaviyo profiles, so you can build targeted social segments, trigger flows to nurture top creators, and bring your best-performing posts into campaigns. Get started for free by capturing email, text, and WhatsApp opt-ins directly from your DMs with Social Auto-replies. Set up a keyword-triggered reply, and when a follower responds, Klaviyo captures their consented email or phone number, so that they’re ready to enter your welcome flow. The paid plan adds even more ways to grow, including Rich social engagement events you can use to segment, trigger flows, and personalize campaigns Webhook events to loyalty platforms, so you can reward top creators and engagers A social content library that centralizes all of your top user-generated content (UGC) and owned posts AI insights that automatically identify your best content and highlight who to partner with next Custom questions to capture preferences and interests from right inside auto-replies One-to-many Instagram account support. Explore Klaviyo Social Marketing now. Everything else from the quarter Those are the headliners, but they aren't the whole story.
